text:
Systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of preoperative methods for predicting difficult tracheal intubation in adult patients without obvious airway abnormalities. Both bedside physical examination tests and ultrasound-based measurements were pooled with bivariate diagnostic meta-analysis methods.

Modified Mallampati test. Pooled from 210 studies involving 532,526 patients with 25,045 difficult intubations: sensitivity 0.39 (95% CI 0.39-0.40), specificity 0.86 (0.86-0.86), positive likelihood ratio 2.29, negative likelihood ratio 0.62, diagnostic odds ratio 5.59 (5.05-6.19), area under the curve 0.7445. Interpretation: high specificity but poor sensitivity — a negative Mallampati does not rule out difficulty, and the test alone is a weak screening tool.

Ultrasound measurements. Distance from skin to epiglottis (US-DSE): 17 studies, 2804 patients, 395 difficult intubations — sensitivity 0.80 (0.75-0.84), specificity 0.77 (0.74-0.79), positive likelihood ratio 3.97. Hyomental distance ratio measured by ultrasound (US-HMDR): diagnostic odds ratio 7.93 (4.37-14.4), AUC 0.7799. Ratio of pre-epiglottic space depth to epiglottis-to-vocal-cord distance (US Pre-E/E-VC) was also evaluated as a predictor. Ultrasound parameters showed better sensitivity than bedside tests.

El-Ganzouri risk index. Eight studies, 13,604 patients, 1017 difficult intubations: sensitivity 0.54 (0.51-0.57), specificity 0.80 (0.80-0.81), positive likelihood ratio 1.79, negative likelihood ratio 1.05, diagnostic odds ratio 1.72 (0.09-31.77), AUC 0.4888 — essentially no discriminative ability in this population.

Clinical interpretation. No single preoperative test predicts difficult intubation reliably on its own. Bedside tests (Mallampati and composite scores) are specific but insensitive; ultrasound airway measurements achieve higher sensitivity and may complement clinical assessment. The authors position ultrasound as a promising adjunct, not a replacement for a structured airway examination, and note heterogeneity and variable cut-off values across studies as limitations. These are diagnostic accuracy statistics, not management recommendations; a predicted difficult airway still requires a planned difficult-airway strategy per local protocol.
title: Evaluation of preoperative difficult airway prediction methods for adult patients without obvious airway abnormalities: a systematic review and meta-analysis
